chunks: A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh, from Nūḥ ibn Shuʿayb, from Abū Dāwūd al-Mustariqq, raising it, said:

Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: The Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله was invited to a meal. When he entered the man’s house, he saw a chicken upon a wall that had laid an egg, and the egg fell upon a peg in the wall and remained fixed upon it; it did not fall and did not break.
The Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله was amazed by it. The man said to him, “Are you amazed by this egg? By the One who sent you with the truth, I have never suffered loss in anything at all.”
He said: Then Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله rose and did not eat anything of his food, and said: “Whoever has not been afflicted with loss, Allah has no need of him.”

key_terms.الْبَيْضَةُ: the egg that became the occasion for amazement
key_terms.حَاجَةٍ: need, concern, or purpose in relation to him
key_terms.رُزِئْتُ: I suffered loss or was afflicted by deprivation
key_terms.طَعَامٍ: a meal or food offered by the host
key_terms.لَمْ يُرْزَأْ: has not been afflicted by loss or trial

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith teach about never experiencing loss or affliction?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a narrative in which the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله responds to a man who boasts of never having suffered any loss or affliction. The narration conveys that being untouched by hardship is not a sign of divine favor; rather, affliction has spiritual significance in a believer’s life. It underscores a moral and theological teaching about trials, divine concern, and the role of suffering.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad bin Abu Abdullah, from Nuh Bin Shuayb, from Abu Dawood Al Mustariq, raising it, said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The Prophet<sup>saww</sup> was invited to a meal. So when he<sup>saww</sup> entered the house of the man, he<sup>saww</sup> looked at a chicken on top of a wall which had laid an egg. So the egg fell upon a crack in the wall, and it was affirmed upon it and did not fall (any further) and did not break.

So the Prophet<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> was astounded from it. So the man said to him<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup>, ‘Are you<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> astounded from this egg? By the One<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Who Sent you<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> with the Truth, I have never had a loss with anything at all’.

So Rasool-Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> arose and did not eat anything from his meal, and said: ‘The one who does not encounter losses/afflictions, so Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> does not Wish to do anything with him’.
en.sarwar: 20. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from Nuh ibn Shu’ayb from abu Dawud al-Mustariqq in a marfu’ manner from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:
“Once, the Holy Prophet was invited for food. When he entered the house he saw a hen that had laid an egg on a wall and it fell on the top of a stake. It stayed there and did not fall off or break.
The Holy Prophet expressed astonishment and the man said, ‘Were you astonished because of this egg? I swear by the One who has sent you with the truth that I have never suffered any loss.’
The Imam said, ‘The Holy Prophet then stood up and left without having any food saying, ‘One who does not suffer any losses, Allah is not interested in him.’”
